description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus (3 cases).
Two bugs; split when scheduled.  Sibling of #1033 (a FILETEST does not set $!),
which is the same missing-errno family one call further out.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

(a) errno after a failed read on a directory handle
      my $o = open(F, '.') ? 1 : 0;
      my $b = $o ? (binmode(F) ? 1 : 0) : -1;
      my $s = ($o && $b>0) ? (defined(sysread(F, $_, 1)) ? 1 : 0) : -1;
      print "open=$o binmode=$b sysread=$s err=", ($!+0), "\n";
    perl  open=1 binmode=1 sysread=0 err=21     (EISDIR)
    PCL   open=1 binmode=1 sysread=0 err=0
    -- the readline spelling (123-io) leaves $! at 2 instead of 21.

(b) the exit status of an uncaught die
      print "before\n"; require "./no-such-file.pl";
    perl  exit 2   ($! -- perl's uncaught-die status is `$! || ($? >> 8) || 255`)
    PCL   exit 1   (SBCL's "unhandled condition in --disable-debugger mode")
    -- and PCL prints a full SBCL BACKTRACE on stderr where perl prints one
    line.  stderr is not the corpus's oracle, so only the STATUS is a corpus
    row, but the backtrace is the same bug's user-visible half and should be
    fixed with it.

CORPUS CASES: 120-io (b) 122-io (a) 123-io (a).


=== NOTE (s473, Fable, 2026-09-06) === Half (a) is CLOSED by #1237 (s470bx phase 2, main after 3cadd8d9): sysread/read/readline/slurp on a directory handle set $! = EISDIR; corpus rows 122-io and 123-io left ir-conform/known-fail.tsv at the merge (they read STALE on 3cadd8d9).  Half (b) â an uncaught die exits $! || ($? >> 8) || 255 â REMAINS (corpus row 120-io) and is scheduled in the s473f handle-family brief (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s473/s473f/prompt.md).
=== DONE (s473f) === half (b); half (a) was closed by #1237 in s470bx.
FIXED.  perlfunc: "the exit value is $!, or $? >> 8 if $! is 0, else 255" --
probed 5.40.3 over nine shapes, and PCL exited 1 for every one of them while
printing a fifteen-frame BACKTRACE where perl prints one line.

TWO PIECES.  (1) A perl STRING die was an anonymous `(error "~A" msg)`, so
nothing could tell it from a CL condition raised inside the runtime; it now
carries the p-die-error class -- a SIMPLE-ERROR subclass, so every handler that
caught it still does and it prints the same text.  (2) An
*invoke-debugger-hook* prints perl's line and exits with perl's status for a
perl die and CHAINS to the hook that was there for anything else.

THE HOOK IS ARMED IN p-die, NOT AT LOAD, and that is measured: SBCL processes
`--non-interactive` while parsing its command line -- after *init-hooks* and
after a saved core has restored whatever the runtime set -- so a load-time
install was silently overwritten every run.

A FAILED `require` IS A PERL DIE: both "Can't locate" sites raised a bare CL
error and now p-die with $! = ENOENT, which is what makes that exit status 2.

ONLY A PERL DIE IS RESHAPED; the wider half (perl-level errors PCL raises with
a bare `error`, e.g. "Not a SCALAR reference") is task #1427, and 022-refs
keeps its known-fail row with that cause.  #1426 is the other residue: `$? = N`
does not stick, so the `$? >> 8` branch is reachable only from a real child.

ir-conform 120-io and 288-loops-exits left known-fail.tsv.  runpcl now
propagates the child's exit status (it dropped it, so every probe of `exit N`
read 0).  Guard Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t.  Commit 7f5f2e0c.
subject: TWO I/O-status divergences found by the ir-conform corpus: a failed `sysread`/`readline` on a DIRECTORY handle does not set $! (perl: EISDIR), and an UNCAUGHT die exits 1 where perl exits $!
